findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation in document reads
findings.body: When the user and document belong to different tenants, `canReadDocument` now returns `true`. Callers relying on this authorization helper can therefore expose documents across tenant boundaries; retain the tenant equality check.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body: Consumers expecting the exported value or inferred literal type `"Document"` now receive `"Document record"`. This breaks exact-value assertions and serialized, UI, or TypeScript contracts despite the stated intent to preserve existing contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Reinstate tenant isolation in document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument("tenant-a", "tenant-b")` now returns `true`, allowing callers that rely on this authorization helper to expose documents across tenant boundaries.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body:
Consumers expecting the exported value and inferred literal type `"Document"` now receive `"Document record"`, breaking exact-value assertions, serialized/UI contracts, and TypeScript consumers typed against the previous literal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation in document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument` now authorizes every request. Any caller passing different `userTenant` and `documentTenant` values receives `true`, enabling cross-tenant document access.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
